speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other mucous membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand the cause, have you ever had a severe bruise or injury that seemed to cause more bleeding than expected?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)

Given the child's age and the classic triad of mucous membrane bleeding (nose, gums), petechiae on the extremities, and easy bruising without a history of severe trauma, I strongly suspect Immune Thrombocytopenia. To confirm this, please provide the results for a Complete Blood Count (CBC) with a Platelet Count and a Peripheral Blood Smear. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_platelet_count, Peripheral_Blood_Smear
